name: Speyside
tagline: The single densest concentration of whisky distilleries anywhere in Scotland, strung along a beautiful river valley.
highlight: Standing in Glenfiddich's original stillhouse as a distiller explains a process barely changed since the distillery's founding in 1886.
shortDescription: Scotland's whisky heartland, home to the highest concentration of distilleries anywhere in the country, strung along the scenic River Spey.
metaDescription: A Speyside travel guide: the Malt Whisky Trail, Glenfiddich, Craigellachie, food and how to plan a visit to Scotland's whisky heartland.

intro: Speyside is genuinely Scotland's whisky heartland, home to the single densest concentration of distilleries found anywhere in the country, strung along the beautiful River Spey valley.

The region produces genuinely more than half of all Scotch whisky, its distinctly smooth, often fruity style shaped by the same river water that also makes the Spey one of the world's most celebrated salmon fishing rivers.

Most visitors genuinely base themselves in or near Dufftown, following the signposted Malt Whisky Trail between distilleries, historic bridges and small towns built almost entirely around whisky's long history here.

whyVisit.intro: Speyside's case rests on genuinely being the single best place in the world to understand and taste Scotch whisky at its source.

points.title: It's genuinely home to the highest distillery density in Scotland
points.text: More working distilleries here than anywhere else in the country, many open for tours.

points.title: The Malt Whisky Trail is genuinely a real, signposted route
points.text: A practical way to visit several distilleries and historic sites without getting lost.

points.title: Glenfiddich is genuinely one of the world's best-known distilleries
points.text: Still family-owned, with a real working history stretching back to 1886.

points.title: The River Spey is genuinely beautiful beyond its whisky connection
points.text: A celebrated salmon river with scenic walking paths along much of its length.

points.title: It works genuinely well alongside the Cairngorms and Loch Ness
points.text: A natural stop on a wider Highland loop, both within easy reach.

attractionsIntro: Speyside's essential sights combine working distilleries with the scenic river valley that shapes them.

attractions.name: Glenfiddich Distillery
attractions.text: Genuinely one of the world's best-known single malt distilleries, still family-owned and operating since 1886.
attractions.tip: Genuinely book a tour ahead — it remains one of the most popular distillery visits in Speyside.

attractions.name: Dufftown Clock Tower

image.file: File:Dufftown clocktower and old jail, Moray.jpg
image.alt: The Clock Tower in Dufftown, Speyside

attractions.text: Genuinely the centrepiece of Dufftown's town square, a Victorian landmark once housing the town's jail.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a good orientation point before setting out to explore the surrounding distilleries.

attractions.name: Craigellachie Bridge

image.alt: Craigellachie Bridge over the River Spey

attractions.text: Genuinely a striking 19th-century iron bridge designed by Thomas Telford, spanning the River Spey in a single dramatic arch.
attractions.tip: Genuinely especially photogenic in autumn, when the surrounding trees turn colour.

attractions.name: The River Spey at Aberlour

image.file: File:Looking downstream on the River Spey at Aberlour - geograph.org.uk - 8167886.jpg
image.alt: The River Spey flowing through Aberlour

attractions.text: Genuinely one of Scotland's most celebrated salmon rivers, its clean water also central to the region's whisky production.
attractions.tip: The genuinely riverside path through Aberlour makes for an easy, scenic walk.

attractions.name: Allt-a-Bhainne Distillery
attractions.text: Genuinely a quieter, less-visited distillery, a good contrast to Speyside's larger, more famous names.
attractions.tip: Genuinely check ahead, as smaller distilleries have more limited public tour schedules.

attractions.name: The Malt Whisky Trail

image.alt: A signpost on the Malt Whisky Trail in Speyside

attractions.text: Genuinely an official signposted route connecting several of Speyside's distilleries and historic sites.
attractions.tip: Genuinely pick up a printed trail map locally to plan a realistic day or two.

attractions.name: Glenfiddich's pagoda roofs

image.alt: The distinctive pagoda roofs of Glenfiddich Distillery

attractions.text: Genuinely one of Speyside's most recognisable architectural details, distinctive kiln roofs found across the region's distilleries.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a great photo opportunity, especially with the surrounding hills as a backdrop.

thingsToDoIntro: Speyside genuinely rewards pacing distillery visits with time along the river itself.

thingsToDo.title: Tour Glenfiddich Distillery
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely thorough introduction to whisky-making, from mash tun to warehouse, ending with a tasting.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely several tour tiers exist, from a basic introduction to more in-depth tasting experiences.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the Speyside Way along the river

image.file: File:Looking upstream on the River Spey at Aberlour - geograph.org.uk - 8167883.jpg
image.alt: Walking the Speyside Way along the River Spey

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely scenic long-distance path following the river, walkable in short, easy sections between towns.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely the Aberlour to Craigellachie stretch is an easy, well-marked introduction to the trail.

thingsToDo.title: Cross Craigellachie Bridge

image.alt: Crossing Craigellachie Bridge over the River Spey

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely quick, worthwhile stop, walking Telford's dramatic iron span over the river below.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely combine with a stop at the nearby distillery of the same name.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Dufftown's old jail

image.alt: The Clock Tower and old jail in Dufftown

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely quick historical stop in the town centre, learning about the tower's varied past uses.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely combine with a wander through Dufftown's small, walkable town centre.

thingsToDo.title: Follow the Malt Whisky Trail

image.alt: Following the Malt Whisky Trail through Speyside

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely practical way to structure a Speyside visit, linking several distilleries by signposted road.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely designate a driver, or use a local tour, given the trail's multiple tasting stops.

thingsToDo.title: Cross the Victoria Footbridge at Aberlour

image.file: File:The Victoria Footbridge over the River Spey at Aberlour - geograph.org.uk - 8167875.jpg
image.alt: The Victoria Footbridge over the River Spey at Aberlour

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely pleasant, easy river crossing on foot, with good views up and down the Spey.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a nice spot to pause and watch for salmon fishers working the river.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Speyside visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book distillery tours genuinely ahead, especially for well-known names like Glenfiddich.
Arrange genuinely a designated driver or organised tour given the region's tastings.
Pick up genuinely a printed Malt Whisky Trail map locally for realistic day planning.
Pack a proper waterproof layer regardless of season for riverside walks.
Book accommodation genuinely ahead during the region's whisky festival periods.
Allow genuinely more time than expected — tastings and tours run longer than a quick stop.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Speyside?
faq.a: Two days genuinely covers Glenfiddich, Dufftown and a stretch of the Speyside Way comfortably.

faq.q: How many distilleries are in Speyside?
faq.a: Genuinely dozens — more working distilleries than anywhere else in Scotland, making it the country's whisky heartland.

faq.q: Do you need to book distillery tours ahead?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely recommended, especially for well-known names like Glenfiddich, which can sell out in peak season.
Genuinely its dense concentration of whisky distilleries and the distinctly smooth, often fruity style of Scotch they produce.

faq.q: Can you visit Speyside without drinking whisky?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — the Speyside Way, Craigellachie Bridge and the region's scenery are worthwhile on their own.

faq.q: How do you get between distilleries safely?
faq.a: Genuinely arrange a designated driver, taxi or organised tour — driving after tastings is never advisable.
